Page: Upper or Lower Antelope Canyon & Glen Canyon Dam and Horseshoe Bend Tour
(244 Reviews)
 Code: PG-11997
 Day Tour
 Page
What To Expect
Overview
Antelope Canyon tickets are included. One-stop tour, professional Navajo guide drive to visit the three major attractions in Page.
Professional guide and best travel planning. The most comfortable way to visit the Upper or Lower or Mountain Sheep Antelope Canyon, Glen Canyon Dam Overlook and Horseshoe Bend.
Pick up and drop off at major hotels in Page by air-conditioned vehicle. For customers arriving on the same day, choose to depart from the Safeway parking lot.
The Antelope Canyon in the morning has a better touring experience, due to fewer tourists. And the Prime Time tour to the Canyon will get better sunlight and take nice pictures.

This tour is a free shuttle from most hotels in downtown Page. It includes a comfortable air-conditioned Van, professional Navajo guide, bottled water, and warm service, which is the most important.

First stop, Antelope Canyon

For this trip, there are three Antelope Canyons to choose from:

Optional item: Upper Antelope Canyon

The Upper Antelope Canyon is called Ts bighnln, the place where water runs through rocks' by the Navajo People in that specific area. It is the most frequently visited by tourists because its entrance and entire length are at ground level. And because beams of direct sunlight radiating down from openings at the top of the canyon are much more common. Beams occur most often in summer, as they require the sun to be high in the sky.

Optional item: Lower Antelope Canyon

The Lower Antelope Canyon, called Hazdistaz, or 'spiral rock arches' by the Navajo, is located several miles from the Upper Antelope Canyon. Prior to the installation of metal stairways, visiting the canyon required climbing pre-installed ladders in certain areas. The lower canyon is in the shape of a "V" and shallower than the Upper Antelope. Lighting is better in the early hours and late morning.

Optional item: Mountain Sheep Slot Canyon

On this particular tour, we will focus on the Mountain Sheep Slot Canyon. This is an off the beaten path trail, lesser known gorge, with a slightly more strenuous hike - which leads to a more private experience than other Slot tours in the area. The canyons are known for their distinctive, undulating walls and its rich, varied colors. It is a popular destination for hikers and photographers, who come to explore its winding corridors and capture its beauty on camera.

The second stop is Horseshoe Bend.

Horseshoe Bend is a superb example of an entrenched meander. Six million years ago, the region around Horseshoe Bend was much closer to sea level, and the Colorado River was a meandering river with a nearly level floodplain. Between six and five million years ago, the region began to be uplifted. This trapped the Colorado River in its bed, and the river rapidly cut downwards to produce Horseshoe Bend as we see it today.

The last stop: Glen Canyon Dam Overlook

A short hike down a set of rock-carved stairs leads to this viewpoint on the rim of the river & dam. This short walk takes you to a viewpoint on the canyon rim high above the Colorado River. It affords an unparalleled view of the river, the canyon, and Glen Canyon Dam. This scenic view provides spectacular vistas of the Colorado River as it flows through Glen Canyon and of Glen Canyon Dam itself. From the parking area, follow the metal handrail down the uneven rock steps.

Finally, we will drive you back to your hotel to finish this pleasant half day tour.

Booking and Confirmation Process
Operator: Roaming Navajo
Booking normally confirmed within 5 minutes if available. In the unlikely event that the inventory runs out, we will send you a cancellation notice and a full refund will be issued shortly. Please check your email.
You will receive your booking information instantly via email. In the event that you do not receive our email, please check your spam folder, or log into your User Center to check your order status and download your voucher when available.
How To Use
Your tour guide will contact you before 8pm the day before departure, to double confirm pickup location and time. If you don't receive a call or SMS, please contact us.
The time to enter Antelope Canyon may be adjusted in advance or delayed by 30 minutes, depending on the capacity of the day.
Please wait for the vehicle at the hotel/departure point 5 minutes in advance. The LOGO on the white vehicle is Roaming Navajo.
Horseshoe Bend will be closed from November 3, 2025, to November 6, 2025. During this period, the half-day tours to Antelope Canyon will cancel the Horseshoe Bend stop. The full-day tours to Antelope Canyon will replace the original Horseshoe Bend itinerary with a visit to Glen Canyon Dam. The tour price will remain unchanged during this period.
